lead: Hyperemesis gravidarum is vomiting through the day in early pregnancy, severe enough to cause dehydration, ketonuria, electrolyte upset and weight loss over 5%. Morning sickness (about half of women, 4–12 wk) and emesis gravidarum (vomiting but hydrated) are milder forms.
f: Cause unclear; main theory is high hCG (peaks at 9–12 wk, like the vomiting) · Multiple and molar pregnancy · Primigravida, previous HG · Thyrotoxicosis

sc: Vomiting at 9 wk, uterus large for dates → Molar pregnancy or twins: scan
Vomiting that starts at 24 wk → Not HG: find the cause

f: Vomiting all day, cannot keep food or fluid down, weight loss, weakness · Blood after retching: Mallory–Weiss tear · Dehydration: dry tongue, poor skin turgor, tachycardia, low BP · PUQE score (hours of nausea, vomits, retching): ≤ 6 diet and oral drugs; 7–11 oral or day-case IV; ≥ 12 admit

Urine ketones; MSU to exclude UTI · FBC (raised Hct), U&E (low Na⁺, K⁺, Cl⁻, raised urea), LFT, TFT, glucose · Ultrasound: viability, twins, molar pregnancy · Acid–base: hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis · Differential: pyelonephritis, gastroenteritis, hepatitis, peptic ulcer, thyrotoxicosis, DKA, raised ICP, red degeneration · Onset after 12 wk, pain, fever or headache = not HG

sc: 10 wk, ketones 3+, Na 128, K 2.9 → Hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis

f: Wernicke encephalopathy (thiamine lack: confusion, ataxia, nystagmus) · Hyponatraemia; corrected too fast → central pontine myelinolysis · Hypokalaemia, Mallory–Weiss tear · VTE (dehydration, immobility) · Liver and renal failure, malnutrition, depression · Fetus: low birth weight; death if Wernicke develops · Low TSH with high free T4 and no goitre = gestational transient thyrotoxicosis: no antithyroid drugs; settles by about 20 wk

sc: On IV dextrose, now confused and ataxic → Wernicke: IV thiamine
Swollen calf on day 4 of admission → DVT: Doppler + LMWH

f: Mild: small dry low-fat meals, reassure (settles by 12–16 wk), oral antiemetic · Admit if she cannot keep down fluid or drugs, ketonuria, weight loss, low K⁺ or Na⁺, or coexisting illness · IV 0.9% saline (or Hartmann's) + KCl by daily U&E · Thiamine 100 mg IV before any dextrose, then oral; add pyridoxine · No hypotonic fluids (worsen low Na⁺) · LMWH and stockings while admitted · Nil by mouth 24–48 h if vomiting everything; fluid chart, weight, U&E, ketones; psychological support

tr: No dextrose before thiamine: it can precipitate Wernicke
Raise sodium by no more than 10 mmol/L in 24 h

f: 1st: promethazine 25 mg or cyclizine 50 mg 8-hourly · 2nd: metoclopramide 10 mg (no longer than 5 days: dystonia) or domperidone · 3rd: ondansetron 4–8 mg · Then hydrocortisone 100 mg IV 12-hourly → oral prednisolone · Then TPN · Termination: last resort when life is at risk · Climb one step only when the step below fails
